title: fix(ldexp): Guard the composite kernel launch onto the operand device
body:
### What does this PR do? → Upon RCA, [ldexp](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/b1aeab3e7b4626cfb833000d0952a91457b726db/aten/src/ATen/native/BinaryOps.cpp#L1599) is `CompositeExplicitAutograd`, so codegen [only emits a device guard for CUDA/XPU keys](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/b1aeab3e7b4626cfb833000d0952a91457b726db/torchgen/gen.py#L216) (`// DeviceGuard omitted`), but its [_ldexp_int_exponent](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/b1aeab3e7b4626cfb833000d0952a91457b726db/aten/src/ATen/native/BinaryOps.cpp#L1574) path launches a device kernel directly through [ldexp_stub](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/b1aeab3e7b4626cfb833000d0952a91457b726db/aten/src/ATen/native/BinaryOps.cpp#L1582) which takes the current thread's stream; so on operands off the current device the launch runs on the wrong context and reads them out of bounds. → Fixed by setting `const OptionalDeviceGuard device_guard(device_of(self))` before the launch, learnt the pattern from how [AmpKernels](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/b1aeab3e7b4626cfb833000d0952a91457b726db/aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/AmpKernels.cu#L50) guards its own un-codegen'd `gpu_kernel`; the `at::mul` fallback already routes through guarded ops so only this path needed it :) Fixes #189567 cc @ptrblck @msaroufim @eqy @tinglvv @nWEIdia ### Verification and Testing → On a 4x L4 (sm_89) box: Was able to reproduce the issue exactly on the unfixed build (`ldexp error vs CPU: 65.62389373779297` on `cuda:1`/`cuda:2`/`cuda:3`, inputs intact), then confirmed the guard restores it to `0.0` on all three. The new multi-GPU test fails without the guard and passes with it; existing `test_ldexp` stays green. ``` python repro.py cuda:1 python test/test_binary_ufuncs.py -k test_ldexp_off_current_device ``` **Before**
**After** ### Environment * `torch` version: `2.14.0a0+gitb1aeab3` (source build, `USE_CUDA=1`, `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=8.9`) * Platform: `Linux-6.8.0-1063-gcp-x86_64-with-glibc2.35`, 48-core x86_64, 188 GB RAM * GPUs: 4x NVIDIA L4 (sm_89, 23 GB each), driver `595.58.03`, CUDA runtime `13.0` * Python version: `3.10.12` * The bug needs an operand device that differs from the current one, so it only shows with >= 2 GPUs; it is invisible on the default `cuda:0` (which is why the reporter never saw it there) and deterministic once triggered. Here it reproduced on `cuda:1`/`cuda:2`/`cuda:3`.
